statements.statement: A school committee member proposed the override be $3 million, saying the difference between $2 million and $3 million is about $200 a year for an average household.
A select board member floated a $4 million override, estimating roughly $800 a year added to an average household's tax bill.
A board member said, citing the DOR website, that a $3 million override would cost the average household about $636 a year.
The finance director stated the current FY26 average single-family tax bill is $7,444, on an average home valued at $517,296.
The finance director stated the impact of a $3 million override would be an additional $63,627 on the average FY26 tax bill (figure as captioned, apparently a decimal-point caption error).
The TriBoard straw-polled with all members present in favor of putting an override question on the ballot at town meeting.
The finance committee chair, presenting a budget diagram, stated projected property tax revenue of $36.3 million as the largest funding source.
The finance committee chair said the FY26 school operating budget relied on one-time free cash, meaning the school started over the sustainable funding line.

The finance committee chair said projected revenue (the funding line) cannot meet the FY27 level-service budget for the town or the schools, meaning services will need to be cut to reach a balanced budget.
A select board member said the core challenge is the structural math and that there is a huge gap the town has to close.
A finance committee member said the town had $1.6 million in unspent/extra funds the past year that could help shrink the level-service ask.
The school committee chair said the committee believed it could have asked for $4 million but did not.
The school committee chair said the committee has stuck to 1.9 (million) for its restoration-budget ask because that is what students need.
Straw poll on override structure: 7 members favored a single override number, 6 (later corrected from 5) favored two tiered override numbers.
A resident reiterated in public comment that a roughly $3 million override averages $636 per household annually.
